topic: The Magic of Text-to-Image AI: Diffusion, CLIP, and the Math Behind It
target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and probability

sections.title: The Big Picture: How AI Dreams
lecture_lines: AI creates images from text descriptions.
This process bridges language and pixels.
CLIP connects text to image meanings.
Diffusion turns noise into sharp images.
These models learn by iterative refinement.

sections.title: Prerequisites: High-Dimensional Spaces
lecture_lines: Images exist in high-dimensional space.
Each pixel contributes to a vector.
Embeddings map features to coordinates.

sections.title: CLIP: The Bridge Between Text and Vision
lecture_lines: CLIP aligns text and image vectors.
Similar items point the same way.
It measures proximity using cosine similarity.
This bridge maps language to vision.
AI interprets your prompt through CLIP.

sections.title: Diffusion Models: The Mathematical Sculptor
lecture_lines: Forward diffusion adds noise to images.
The reverse process removes noise.
Neural networks predict the noise.
Iterative denoising reveals the image.
This sculpted noise creates structure.

sections.title: Guiding the Process: The Mathematics of Condition
lecture_lines: Text embeddings guide the denoising.
They act as a semantic magnet.
Pixels align with requested descriptions.
